exports.name: clampQuantity
exports.doc: Clamps a quantity to at least 1 and at most upper.

exports.name: lineTotal
exports.doc:
The amount of a line item. The quantity is clamped before multiplying, so a negative quantity never
makes the amount negative.

exports.name: lineTotals
exports.signature: (unitPrice : Int53, quantities : Array Int53) → Array Int53
exports.declaration: lineTotals(unitPrice: number, quantities: readonly number[]): readonly number[]
exports.doc: The amount of every line of an order at one unit price.

exports.name: anyOverLimit
exports.declaration: anyOverLimit(amounts: readonly number[], limit: number): boolean

exports.name: firstOverLimit
exports.signature: (amounts : Array Int53, limit : Int53) → Option Int53
exports.declaration: firstOverLimit(amounts: readonly number[], limit: number): Option<number>
exports.doc: The first line that breaks the limit. Lines after it are never looked at.

exports.name: everyLineWithinLimit
exports.declaration: everyLineWithinLimit(amounts: readonly number[], limit: number): boolean

exports.name: pageOf
exports.signature: (xs : Array Int53, lo : Int53, hi : Int53) → Array Int53
exports.declaration: pageOf(xs: readonly number[], lo: number, hi: number): readonly number[]
exports.doc: One window of a list. A window reaching past the end is refused rather than shortened.

exports.name: combinedCart
exports.signature: (saved : Array Int53, added : Array Int53) → Array Int53
exports.declaration: combinedCart(saved: readonly number[], added: readonly number[]): readonly number[]

exports.name: headOr
exports.declaration: headOr(xs: readonly number[], fallback: number): number
exports.doc: An out-of-range read traps rather than yielding `undefined`.

exports.name: orderReference
exports.doc: The reference an order is filed under: the prefix and the order number in decimal.

exports.name: amountOf
exports.doc:
The amount a line carries, read back from the string the caller was handed. `none` unless the
string is exactly the decimal spelling of an Int53, so `"007"`, `" 5"` and `"+5"` are refused.

exports.name: amountOr
exports.doc: The same amount, with a fallback for a field that does not spell one.

exports.name: separatorAt
exports.doc:
Where the separator first sits in a reference, counted in code points. `none` when the reference
carries none. JS's own `indexOf` counts UTF-16 units and answers `-1`.

exports.name: referencePrefix
exports.doc: The part of a reference before its first separator, or the whole reference when it carries none.

exports.name: joinFields
exports.declaration: joinFields(fields: readonly string[], separator: string): string
exports.doc:
A row of an uploaded file written back out: the fields in order with the separator between them.
An empty list of fields writes an empty row.

exports.name: referenceFrom
exports.doc:
The reference an order is filed under, built from parts that are already in hand, under the same
separator `referencePrefix` reads back.

exports.name: refiled
exports.signature: (reference : String, oldSep : String, newSep : String) → String
exports.declaration: refiled(reference: string, oldSep: string, newSep: string): string
exports.doc:
A reference filed under one separator, rewritten under another. Every occurrence moves, and a
reference carrying none comes back unchanged.

exports.name: receiptRule
exports.doc:
The rule a printed receipt puts between its sections: `mark` written out 32 times, which is one
column each where `mark` is a single character.

exports.name: amountColumn
exports.doc:
An amount in minor units, right-aligned in the column a printed receipt gives it. Too wide an
amount keeps its digits and overruns the column.

exports.name: lineNumbers
exports.doc:
The line numbers a printed receipt gives its rows, counting from one. The count is clamped: a
receipt prints at most `maxReceiptRows` rows, and `Arr.range` asks that the text bound how far it
counts.

exports.name: sortsBefore
exports.doc: Comparison in code point order. JS's `<` compares UTF-16 units, so it does not agree.

exports.name: mentionsTerm
exports.doc: Whether a free-text note mentions a search term, ignoring case.

exports.name: storedCoupon
exports.doc:
A coupon code as it is stored: the campaign prefix and what the customer typed, upper-cased and with
the surrounding whitespace gone.

exports.name: couponApplies
exports.doc: Whether a coupon belongs to a campaign, comparing the way the codes are stored.

exports.name: fieldCount
exports.doc:
How many columns a line of an uploaded file carries. An empty separator leaves the line whole rather
than cutting it into characters.

exports.name: truncateLabel
exports.doc:
A label cut to fit, counted in code points so a surrogate pair is never split in half. A negative
limit has no string to return and fails the way an out-of-range index does.

exports.name: isSpreadsheet
exports.doc: Whether an uploaded file is a spreadsheet, compared the way the names are stored.

exports.name: limitsFor
exports.doc: What a role may do in a day and in a month.

exports.name: priceOf
exports.signature: (prices : Dict Int53, sku : String) → Option Int53
exports.declaration: priceOf(prices: ReadonlyMap<string, number>, sku: string): Option<number>

exports.name: isListed
exports.declaration: isListed(prices: ReadonlyMap<string, number>, sku: string): boolean

exports.name: repriced
exports.signature: (prices : Dict Int53, sku : String, amount : Int53) → Dict Int53
exports.declaration: repriced(prices: ReadonlyMap<string, number>, sku: string, amount: number): ReadonlyMap<string, number>
exports.doc: The price book after one price change. A sku already in the book keeps its place.

exports.name: withdrawn
exports.signature: (prices : Dict Int53, sku : String) → Dict Int53
exports.declaration: withdrawn(prices: ReadonlyMap<string, number>, sku: string): ReadonlyMap<string, number>
exports.doc: The price book after a sku is withdrawn. A sku that was never listed leaves the book unchanged.

exports.name: objPriceOf
exports.signature: (prices : Dict.Obj Int53, sku : String) → Option Int53
exports.declaration: objPriceOf(prices: ReadonlyMap<string, number> | { readonly [key: string]: number }, sku: string): Option<number>

exports.name: objIsListed
exports.declaration: objIsListed(prices: ReadonlyMap<string, number> | { readonly [key: string]: number }, sku: string): boolean

exports.name: objRepriced
exports.signature: (prices : Dict.Obj Int53, sku : String, amount : Int53) → Dict.Obj Int53
exports.declaration: objRepriced(prices: ReadonlyMap<string, number> | { readonly [key: string]: number }, sku: string, amount: number): { readonly [key: string]: number }
exports.doc:
The price book after one price change, handed back as an object. A sku already in the book keeps its
place.

exports.name: objWithdrawn
exports.signature: (prices : Dict.Obj Int53, sku : String) → Dict.Obj Int53
exports.declaration: objWithdrawn(prices: ReadonlyMap<string, number> | { readonly [key: string]: number }, sku: string): { readonly [key: string]: number }
exports.doc: The price book after a sku is withdrawn, handed back as an object.

exports.name: objListedSkus
exports.declaration: objListedSkus(prices: ReadonlyMap<string, number> | { readonly [key: string]: number }): readonly string[]

exports.name: objListedPrices
exports.declaration: objListedPrices(prices: ReadonlyMap<string, number> | { readonly [key: string]: number }): readonly number[]

exports.name: objCatalogueSize
exports.declaration: objCatalogueSize(prices: ReadonlyMap<string, number> | { readonly [key: string]: number }): number

exports.name: objLimitsFor
exports.doc:
What a role may do, written out at the spelling that crosses as a plain object rather than as a
`Map`. Beside `limitsFor` it is one dictionary written twice: the same entries, the same operations, and
what the spelling decides is only what a consumer is handed.

exports.name: divide
exports.doc: Truncating division. Division by zero traps on the JS side too.

exports.name: taxOn
exports.doc:
The tax on an amount in minor units at a rate in basis points, rounded half away from zero — which
is the rounding an amount of money gets where nothing says otherwise.

exports.name: shareOf
exports.doc:
What each of `parties` carries of a cost, rounded up. A count of zero or less is read as one, since
a cost carried by nobody is carried by the one who has it.

exports.name: evenShare
exports.doc:
One party's share of an amount split evenly, rounded to the nearest whole unit with a half going
away from zero. A count of zero or less is read as one, as `shareOf` reads it.

exports.name: dayOfInstant
exports.doc:
Which whole day an instant falls in, counting from the epoch, where an instant before it belongs to
the day it is inside rather than to the one after: `divFloor` and not `div`.

exports.name: dayNumber
exports.signature: (year : Int53, month : Int53, day : Int53) → Int53
exports.declaration: dayNumber(year: number, month: number, day: number): number
exports.doc: The day a calendar date falls on, counting from 1970-01-01.

exports.name: yearOf
exports.doc: The calendar year a day number falls in.

exports.name: monthOf
exports.doc: The calendar month a day number falls in, 1 through 12.

exports.name: dayOfMonthOf
exports.doc: The day of the month a day number falls on, 1 through 31.

exports.name: weekdayOf
exports.doc: The day of the week a day number falls on, 0 for Sunday through 6 for Saturday.

exports.name: monthLength
exports.doc: How many days a calendar month holds, a leap February included.

exports.name: discounted
exports.doc: The amount after a percent% discount. The remainder is truncated.

exports.name: rebindTwice
exports.doc:
Binds the same name twice. ESM runs in strict mode, so emitting `const` twice would fail at import
time.

exports.name: clampChannel
exports.signature: (value : UInt32, lo : UInt32, hi : UInt32) → UInt32
exports.declaration: clampChannel(value: number, lo: number, hi: number): number
exports.doc: A channel value held between a floor and a ceiling.

exports.name: safeQuotientIsPositive
exports.doc: Doubles as a check on short-circuiting. When `b` is 0 the right-hand side is not evaluated.

exports.name: canCheckout
exports.signature: (signedIn : Bool, cartTotal : Int53, stock : Int53) → Bool
exports.declaration: canCheckout(signedIn: boolean, cartTotal: number, stock: number): boolean

exports.name: addMoney
exports.signature: (a : Money, b : Money) → Result Money String
exports.declaration: addMoney(a: Money, b: Money): Result<Money, string>
exports.doc:
Amounts in different currencies cannot be added. `===` is unusable on the JS side, so a structural
equality helper is called.

exports.name: cartTotal
exports.doc:
Adds the amounts up whatever currency each carries; `addMoney` is the operation that refuses to mix
them.

exports.name: cheapestFirst
exports.doc: The lines of a cart, cheapest first. Lines that cost the same keep the order they came in.

exports.name: inLabelOrder
exports.doc: Labels in the order the subset compares strings, which counts code points.

exports.name: refundableOnly
exports.signature: (role : Role, states : Array OrderState) → Array OrderState
exports.declaration: refundableOnly(role: Role, states: readonly OrderState[]): readonly OrderState[]
exports.doc: The orders this role may still refund. The predicate reads `role` from outside the lambda.

exports.name: ship
exports.signature: (state : OrderState, trackingId : String) → Result OrderState String
exports.declaration: ship(state: OrderState, trackingId: string): Result<OrderState, string>
exports.doc: The state transition to shipped. Rejects states that cannot transition and an empty tracking id.

exports.name: quantityLabel
exports.doc: The label shown next to a line item.

exports.name: renewalLabel
exports.doc: Whether a subscription carries on. Both cases are named, so no fallback is needed.

exports.name: chargeable
exports.doc:
An amount of zero is free whatever the currency, and an amount carrying no currency cannot be
charged at all.

exports.name: settleMessage
exports.doc:
The shipping line shown once a transition has been attempted. A draft or cancelled order has nothing
to show, so one arm reaches past `ok` and leaves the state itself open.

exports.name: settledOrderId
exports.doc:
The order the settlement placed, if it placed one. The wildcard here stands for both the states that
are not `placed` and the error, so the split the certificate makes reaches `Except` as well.

exports.name: dailyLimit
exports.doc: A role with no daily limit recorded may do nothing.

exports.name: monthlyLimit
exports.doc:
The same read with the arms the other way round: an arm that binds, then a wildcard for the rest.
The certificate splits the scrutinee to show the binding arm did not fire, which `Option` needs as much
as a type the program declares.

exports.name: remainingItems
exports.doc: How many results lie beyond the page in hand.

exports.name: firstPage
exports.doc: The whole list served as a single page.

exports.name: validateQuantity
exports.doc: Accepts an order quantity or says why it was refused.

exports.name: validationMessage
exports.doc: The line shown once a quantity has been checked.

exports.name: amountWithTax
exports.doc: The amount and the tax charged on it, as the two lines they are billed as.

exports.name: previewLines
exports.signature: (amounts : Array Int53, upTo : Int53) → Array Int53
exports.declaration: previewLines(amounts: readonly number[], upTo: number): readonly number[]
exports.doc:
The lines shown before the fold. A count past the end of the order shows the whole of it, where
`pageOf` would have refused the window.

exports.name: linesBelowFold
exports.signature: (amounts : Array Int53, upTo : Int53) → Array Int53
exports.declaration: linesBelowFold(amounts: readonly number[], upTo: number): readonly number[]

exports.name: stocksSku
exports.declaration: stocksSku(skus: readonly string[], sku: string): boolean

exports.name: allLines
exports.doc: Every line of every order in one list.

exports.name: priceOr
exports.signature: (prices : Dict Int53, sku : String, fallback : Int53) → Int53
exports.declaration: priceOr(prices: ReadonlyMap<string, number>, sku: string, fallback: number): number
exports.doc: The listed price, or the fallback where the sku is not in the book.

exports.name: byCurrency
exports.doc: One line per currency. Where a currency appears twice the later line is the one kept.

exports.name: settledOrElse
exports.signature: (outcome : Result Money String, fallback : Money) → Money
exports.declaration: settledOrElse(outcome: Result<Money, string>, fallback: Money): Money

exports.name: settledCurrency
exports.signature: (outcome : Result Money String) → Result String String

exports.name: loudRefusal
exports.signature: (outcome : Result Money String) → Result Money String
exports.doc: The refusal upper-cased. What the settlement accepted is handed back untouched.

exports.name: trackingIds
exports.doc:
The tracking id of every order that has one, and an empty string for the rest. The `match` is inside
the traversal's own function rather than in a declaration of its own.

exports.name: refundCount
exports.doc: How many of the amounts are refunds, with the test written where the count is.

exports.name: creditNoteAmount
exports.doc: A charge as it appears on a credit note, where money leaving is written negative.

exports.name: directionLabel
exports.doc: What the sign on a statement line means.

exports.name: directChildren
exports.doc:
How many categories sit directly under this one. What sits under *those* is a walk, which is what
`categoryProducts` takes.

exports.name: categoryProducts
exports.doc:
How many products the catalogue holds, however deep the groups go. A group answers for everything
under it, so this walks the whole tree rather than reading one level of it.

theorems.name: add_comm
theorems.statement: add_comm (a b : Int) : add a b = add b a
theorems.doc:
Swapping the arguments of `add` changes nothing: whatever the two integers, both orders give the same
sum.

theorems.name: cheapest_first_keeps_every_line
theorems.statement: cheapest_first_keeps_every_line (items : List Money) : (cheapestFirst items).Perm items
theorems.doc:
Ordering a cart by price loses no line and invents none: the answer holds the same lines as the
cart it was given, in some order.

theorems.name: monthly_limit_is_not_negative
theorems.statement: monthly_limit_is_not_negative (role : Role) : 0 ≤ monthlyLimit role
theorems.doc: No role's monthly limit is negative, including a role whose book records none.

theorems.name: nothing_under_it_counts_none
theorems.statement:
nothing_under_it_counts_none (name : String) :
  directChildren (Category.leaf name) = 0 ∧ directChildren (Category.group name []) = 0
theorems.doc:
A category with nothing under it counts nothing under it, whatever it is called. Two shapes have
nothing under them — a leaf, and a group holding no categories — and both are here.

theorems.name: a_group_counts_what_is_directly_under_it
theorems.statement:
a_group_counts_what_is_directly_under_it (name : String) (children : List Category) :
  directChildren (Category.group name children) = Arr.length children
theorems.doc: A group counts what sits directly under it, however deep those categories go themselves.

theorems.name: a_leaf_holds_one_product
theorems.statement: a_leaf_holds_one_product (name : String) : categoryProducts (Category.leaf name) = 1
theorems.doc: A leaf holds one product, whatever it is called.

theorems.name: an_empty_group_holds_no_product
theorems.statement: an_empty_group_holds_no_product (name : String) : categoryProducts (Category.group name []) = 0
theorems.doc: A group is not itself a product: a group with nothing under it holds none.

theorems.name: nesting_keeps_the_product
theorems.statement:
nesting_keeps_the_product (outer inner product : String) :
  categoryProducts (Category.group outer [Category.group inner [Category.leaf product]]) = 1
theorems.doc:
The walk goes past the first level, which is the whole difference from `directChildren`: a group
whose only child is a group holding one leaf holds that one product.

theorems.name: a_group_holds_what_its_children_hold
theorems.statement:
a_group_holds_what_its_children_hold (name : String) (children : List Category) :
  categoryProducts (Category.group name children) = Arr.sum (List.map categoryProducts children)
theorems.doc:
A group holds what its children hold and nothing besides: the count distributes over the children,
however deep each of them goes.

theorems.name: failed_settlement_has_no_order_id
theorems.statement: failed_settlement_has_no_order_id (message : String) : settledOrderId (Except.error message) = 0
theorems.doc: A settlement that failed carries no order id, whatever it failed with.

theorems.name: line_total_caps_the_quantity
theorems.statement:
line_total_caps_the_quantity (unitPrice quantity : Int) (hq : maxLineQuantity < quantity) :
  lineTotal unitPrice quantity = unitPrice * maxLineQuantity
theorems.doc: A line ordered past the cap is billed at the cap, whatever the unit price.

theorems.name: reference_from_three_parts
theorems.statement: reference_from_three_parts (a b c : String) : referenceFrom [a, b, c] = a ++ "-" ++ b ++ "-" ++ c
theorems.doc:
Three parts come out of `referenceFrom` in the order they went in, with a hyphen written between each
neighbouring pair. Hyphens the parts themselves carry are not counted, so this says nothing about how many
the answer holds.

theorems.name: line_numbers_counts_the_rows
theorems.statement: line_numbers_counts_the_rows (rows : Int) : Arr.length (lineNumbers rows) = min (max rows 0) maxReceiptRows
theorems.doc:
A receipt numbers one row per row it prints: as many numbers as the clamped count says, whatever
`rows` was asked for.

theorems.name: line_numbers_are_rows
theorems.statement: line_numbers_are_rows (rows k : Int) : k ∈ lineNumbers rows ↔ 1 ≤ k ∧ k ≤ min (max rows 0) maxReceiptRows
theorems.doc:
The numbers a receipt prints are exactly the rows it has: a number is one of them when it is at
least 1 and at most the clamped count, and is not one of them otherwise.

theorems.name: draft_never_ships
theorems.statement:
draft_never_ships (trackingId : String) :
  evalCall program "ship" [Value.obj "draft" [], Value.str trackingId] =
    Except.ok (Value.obj "error" [("error", Value.str "a draft order cannot ship")])
theorems.doc: A draft order cannot ship, whatever tracking id comes with it.

theorems.name: clamped_quantity_in_range
theorems.statement:
clamped_quantity_in_range (quantity : Int) (hlo : int53Min ≤ quantity) (hhi : quantity ≤ int53Max) :
  ∃ n,
    evalCall program "clampQuantity" [Value.int53 quantity, Value.int53 999] = Except.ok (Value.int53 n) ∧
      1 ≤ n ∧ n ≤ 999
theorems.doc: Clamping any `Int53` quantity to at most 999 lands between 1 and 999.

theorems.name: same_currency_adds
theorems.statement:
same_currency_adds (x y : Int) (currency : String) (hx : int53Min ≤ x ∧ x ≤ int53Max) (hy : int53Min ≤ y ∧ y ≤ int53Max)
  (hsum : int53Min ≤ x + y ∧ x + y ≤ int53Max) :
  evalCall program "addMoney" [money x currency, money y currency] =
    Except.ok (Value.obj "ok" [("value", money (x + y) currency)])
theorems.doc: Two amounts in the same currency add up, as long as their sum stays within `Int53`.

theorems.name: program_typesNoDictObj
theorems.statement: program_typesNoDictObj : program.typesNoDictObj = true
theorems.doc:
No type this program declares carries a dictionary the declaration told the compiler to hand across
the boundary as a plain object rather than as a `Map`. This is the half `encodeAt` reads — it recurses
into a declared type's fields and never into a declaration — so every claim below whose own return type
reaches no such dictionary is stated at `encodeValue`, the spelling it has always had, through
`encodeAt_eq_encodeValue`.

The program itself does hand one across: `objRepriced` and `objWithdrawn` return a `Dict.Obj Int`, so
their entries emit the walk out that `Compile.retWalk` expands and their results are read at `encodeAt`
rather than at `encodeValue`. Every other `obj` declaration takes one and returns something that reaches
none, so its entry emits no walk and this theorem carries it to `encodeValue` like any other.

theorems.name: add_calls_agree
theorems.statement:
add_calls_agree [Discriminators] (m : Js.Module) (hm : Compile.compileProgram program = Except.ok m)
  (jargs : List Js.JsValue) (args : List Value) (v : Value) (hdec : Decl.ArgsDecode program addDecl.params jargs args)
  (he : evalCall program "add" args = Except.ok v) :
  ∃ g, ∀ (g' : Nat), g ≤ g' → Js.callFunctionAt m g' "add" jargs = Except.ok (encodeValue v)
theorems.doc:
Whatever arguments the entry check accepts, the generated `add` returns what `eval` returns. Its body
is a single binary operation.

theorems.name: discounted_calls_agree
theorems.statement:
discounted_calls_agree [Discriminators] (m : Js.Module) (hm : Compile.compileProgram program = Except.ok m)
  (jargs : List Js.JsValue) (args : List Value) (v : Value)
  (hdec : Decl.ArgsDecode program discountedDecl.params jargs args)
  (he : evalCall program "discounted" args = Except.ok v) :
  ∃ g, ∀ (g' : Nat), g ≤ g' → Js.callFunctionAt m g' "discounted" jargs = Except.ok (encodeValue v)
theorems.doc: The same for a body that opens with a `let`, which the compiler emits as a `const` statement.

theorems.name: rebindTwice_calls_agree
theorems.statement:
rebindTwice_calls_agree [Discriminators] (m : Js.Module) (hm : Compile.compileProgram program = Except.ok m)
  (jargs : List Js.JsValue) (args : List Value) (v : Value)
  (hdec : Decl.ArgsDecode program rebindTwiceDecl.params jargs args)
  (he : evalCall program "rebindTwice" args = Except.ok v) :
  ∃ g, ∀ (g' : Nat), g ≤ g' → Js.callFunctionAt m g' "rebindTwice" jargs = Except.ok (encodeValue v)
theorems.doc:
And for a body whose second `let` rebinds a name already in scope, which the compiler leaves as an
expression rather than a statement.

theorems.name: memberPrice_calls_agree
theorems.statement:
memberPrice_calls_agree [Discriminators] (m : Js.Module) (hm : Compile.compileProgram program = Except.ok m)
  (jargs : List Js.JsValue) (args : List Value) (v : Value)
  (hdec : Decl.ArgsDecode program memberPriceDecl.params jargs args)
  (he : evalCall program "memberPrice" args = Except.ok v) :
  ∃ g, ∀ (g' : Nat), g ≤ g' → Js.callFunctionAt m g' "memberPrice" jargs = Except.ok (encodeValue v)
theorems.doc:
And for a body that calls another declaration, handing it a third by name. The call is where the
proof leaves the expression it is looking at: `priced` applies the function it was given, so the claim
about `memberPrice` rests on the same claim about `tenPercentOff`.

theorems.name: program_progOk
theorems.statement: program_progOk : Cost.progOk program = true
theorems.doc:
The first of the two checks the emitter runs on a program before it writes anything: every call goes
backwards.

theorems.name: program_cost_fits
theorems.statement: program_cost_fits : Cost.cost program ≤ defaultFuel
theorems.doc: The second: the fuel the artifact runs at covers the deepest call this program can make.

theorems.name: add_traps
theorems.statement:
add_traps [Discriminators] (m : Js.Module) (hm : Compile.compileProgram program = Except.ok m) (jargs : List Js.JsValue)
  (args : List Value) (err : Err) (htyped : ParamsTyped program addDecl.params args)
  (hdec : Decl.ArgsDecode program addDecl.params jargs args) (he : evalCall program "add" args = Except.error err) :
  ∃ g, ∀ (g' : Nat), g ≤ g' → Js.callFunctionAt m g' "add" jargs = Except.error err.code
theorems.doc:
For arguments the entry check decodes to the count and types `add` declares, whenever `eval` refuses
to return a value the generated function throws the code `eval` threw. Its body can reach `int53Overflow`.
Running out of fuel is not among the answers: the two checks above rule it out for this program. What
falls outside those types never reaches the body at all — that is `add_refuses`.

theorems.name: add_overflow_throws
theorems.statement:
add_overflow_throws [Discriminators] (m : Js.Module) (hm : Compile.compileProgram program = Except.ok m) :
  ∃ g,
    ∀ (g' : Nat),
      g ≤ g' → Js.callFunctionAt m g' "add" [Js.JsValue.num int53Max, Js.JsValue.num 1] = Except.error "int53Overflow"
theorems.doc:
The trap is reachable, and reached the same way on both sides: one past the top of `Int53` throws
`int53Overflow` out of the generated function.

theorems.name: addMoney_calls_agree
theorems.statement:
addMoney_calls_agree [Discriminators] (m : Js.Module) (hm : Compile.compileProgram program = Except.ok m)
  (jargs : List Js.JsValue) (args : List Value) (v : Value)
  (hdec : Decl.ArgsDecode program addMoneyDecl.params jargs args)
  (he : evalCall program "addMoney" args = Except.ok v) :
  ∃ g, ∀ (g' : Nat), g ≤ g' → Js.callFunctionAt m g' "addMoney" jargs = Except.ok (encodeValue v)
theorems.doc:
The fragment reaches business logic, not just arithmetic: `addMoney` reads two fields, compares them,
and builds a `Result` around a constructor.

theorems.name: ship_calls_agree
theorems.statement:
ship_calls_agree [Discriminators] (m : Js.Module) (hm : Compile.compileProgram program = Except.ok m)
  (jargs : List Js.JsValue) (args : List Value) (v : Value) (hdec : Decl.ArgsDecode program shipDecl.params jargs args)
  (he : evalCall program "ship" args = Except.ok v) :
  ∃ g, ∀ (g' : Nat), g ≤ g' → Js.callFunctionAt m g' "ship" jargs = Except.ok (encodeValue v)
theorems.doc:
The fragment reaches a `match`: `ship` chooses an arm by the constructor of its scrutinee and reads
the fields that arm binds.

theorems.name: cartTotal_calls_agree
theorems.statement:
cartTotal_calls_agree [Discriminators] (m : Js.Module) (hm : Compile.compileProgram program = Except.ok m)
  (jargs : List Js.JsValue) (args : List Value) (v : Value)
  (hdec : Decl.ArgsDecode program cartTotalDecl.params jargs args)
  (he : evalCall program "cartTotal" args = Except.ok v) :
  ∃ g, ∀ (g' : Nat), g ≤ g' → Js.callFunctionAt m g' "cartTotal" jargs = Except.ok (encodeValue v)
theorems.doc: And an array traversal: `cartTotal` folds a body over the elements, each under its own binding.

theorems.name: cartTotal_traps
theorems.statement:
cartTotal_traps [Discriminators] (m : Js.Module) (hm : Compile.compileProgram program = Except.ok m)
  (jargs : List Js.JsValue) (args : List Value) (err : Err) (htyped : ParamsTyped program cartTotalDecl.params args)
  (hdec : Decl.ArgsDecode program cartTotalDecl.params jargs args)
  (he : evalCall program "cartTotal" args = Except.error err) :
  ∃ g, ∀ (g' : Nat), g ≤ g' → Js.callFunctionAt m g' "cartTotal" jargs = Except.error err.code
theorems.doc:
The trap side of a traversal: a fold whose running sum leaves `Int53` throws where `eval` does, at
the element that overflowed rather than at the end.

theorems.name: add_refuses
theorems.statement:
add_refuses [Discriminators] (m : Js.Module) (hm : Compile.compileProgram program = Except.ok m)
  (jargs : List Js.JsValue) (hk : Js.dictKeysDistinctList jargs = true)
  (hno : ¬Decl.EvalAccepts program addDecl jargs) : Js.callFunction m "add" jargs = Except.error "typeError"
theorems.doc:
Whatever `add` is handed, if no reading of those JS values is a pair of `Int53`s, the generated
function throws instead of computing. The one shape left out is a dictionary holding a key twice, which a
`Map` cannot hold.

theorems.name: add_refuses_string
theorems.statement:
add_refuses_string [Discriminators] (m : Js.Module) (hm : Compile.compileProgram program = Except.ok m) :
  Js.callFunction m "add" [Js.JsValue.str "1", Js.JsValue.num 2] = Except.error "typeError"
theorems.doc:
The hypothesis discharged on a concrete call: a string where an `Int53` was declared throws, because
no `Int53` encodes to one.

theorems.name: addMoney_traps
theorems.statement:
addMoney_traps [Discriminators] (m : Js.Module) (hm : Compile.compileProgram program = Except.ok m)
  (jargs : List Js.JsValue) (args : List Value) (err : Err) (htyped : ParamsTyped program addMoneyDecl.params args)
  (hdec : Decl.ArgsDecode program addMoneyDecl.params jargs args)
  (he : evalCall program "addMoney" args = Except.error err) :
  ∃ g, ∀ (g' : Nat), g ≤ g' → Js.callFunctionAt m g' "addMoney" jargs = Except.error err.code
theorems.doc:
The same for `addMoney`, under the same declared types: the only way its body throws is the `Int53`
overflow of the sum, and the generated function throws that code.

theorems.name: file_reads_back
theorems.statement:
file_reads_back [Discriminators] (m : Js.Module) (hm : Compile.compileProgram program = Except.ok m) :
  Parse.parseModule m.render.toList = some m
theorems.doc:
The text `lean2js` writes for this program reads back as the module the compiler built. Nothing in
between is assumed: the roundtrip holds of whatever `compileProgram` produces, so the claim carries no
side condition about the shape of the module.

theorems.name: helpers_ship_as_modelled
theorems.statement:
helpers_ship_as_modelled (ext : HelperSem.Ext) (name : String) (args : List Js.JsValue) (r : Js.JsResult)
  (hok : HelperSem.helperArgsOk name args) (h : Js.helper name args = some r) :
  HelperSem.Helper.Calls ext name (List.map HelperSem.ofJs args) (HelperSem.ofRes r)
theorems.doc:
The runtime helpers are the last hand-written JavaScript in the artifact, and the model of the
generated code reaches most of them through one table. Every row of that table is what the source the
compiler prints actually computes; `helperArgsOk` is what a call to a row is still asked for, and it asks
only for the Int53 range a type has already given, the distinct keys a `Map` cannot break, and the shapes
on which `__eq`'s walk and the model's structural equality decide the same thing.

`__ck` and the seven traversal helpers are not rows: the model evaluates them as rules of its own, and
`HelperProof` answers those against the same printed source.

theorems.name: entry_check_fits_dts
theorems.statement:
entry_check_fits_dts (jv : Js.JsValue) (ty : Ty) (b : Nat) (d : Js.TyDesc)
  (hd : Compile.tyDesc program b ty = Except.ok d) (hc : Js.checkTy [] jv d = true) : Dts.TsSat program ty jv
theorems.doc:
Everything the entry check lets through is a value admitted by the type the published `.d.ts` prints
for that parameter. The two are not the same set: the check reads a number's range, which a TypeScript
type cannot say, so a call the `.d.ts` accepts can still be refused at the boundary.

theorems.name: dts_fits_entry_check
theorems.statement:
dts_fits_entry_check [Discriminators] (m : Js.Module) (hm : Compile.compileProgram program = Except.ok m)
  (jv : Js.JsValue) (ty : Ty) (b : Nat) (d : Js.TyDesc) (hd : Compile.tyDesc program b ty = Except.ok d)
  (hts : Dts.TsSat program ty jv) (hr : Dts.inRange [] jv d = true) : Js.checkTy [] jv d = true
theorems.doc:
The other direction, and the one a caller feels: an argument the published `.d.ts` type admits is one
the entry check accepts. `Dts.inRange` is the whole of what is assumed about the value — the `Int53` and
`UInt32` ranges the check reads, which a TypeScript type cannot express. The order the keys arrive in is
not read, and neither are keys the type does not declare.

theorems.name: encoded_values_fit_dts
theorems.statement:
encoded_values_fit_dts [Discriminators] (m : Js.Module) (hm : Compile.compileProgram program = Except.ok m) (v : Value)
  (ty : Ty) (hv : Value.hasTy program v ty = true) : Dts.TsSatOut program ty (encodeAt program ty v)
theorems.doc:
What comes back, rather than what goes in: a value the reference semantics gives a declared type to,
read out through that type, is one the published `.d.ts` admits at the type it prints for a *return*,
which is the narrower of the two where the type reaches a dictionary crossing as a plain object.
`typeSound` gives the type to whatever a declaration returns, and `decl_correct` says the generated
function returns exactly that reading — so this is the value a consumer meets. Where the type reaches no
such dictionary the reading is the encoding itself (`encodeAt_eq_encodeValue`,
`program_typesNoDictObj`).

theorems.name: returned_values_fit_parameter_types
theorems.statement:
returned_values_fit_parameter_types (ty : Ty) (jv : Js.JsValue) (h : Dts.TsSatOut program ty jv) :
  Dts.TsSat program ty jv
theorems.doc:
The type the `.d.ts` prints for a return is one the type it prints for a parameter admits, so a call
chained onto another type-checks. That is a statement about the two printed types and nothing else; that
the value is *accepted* at run time is `returned_values_pass_the_entry_check`. This is what lets
`encoded_values_fit_dts` be handed to `dts_fits_entry_check`.

theorems.name: returned_values_pass_the_entry_check
theorems.statement:
returned_values_pass_the_entry_check [Discriminators] (m : Js.Module)
  (hm : Compile.compileProgram program = Except.ok m) (v : Value) (ty : Ty) (b : Nat) (d : Js.TyDesc)
  (hd : Compile.tyDesc program b ty = Except.ok d) (hv : Value.hasTy program v ty = true) :
  Js.checkTy [] (encodeAt program ty v) d = true
theorems.doc:
And it is accepted, not merely admitted by the type: what one call hands back passes the next call's
entry check, with none of the range caveat `dts_fits_entry_check` carries. The range is what
`Value.hasTy` already says about the value the first call returned, so two exported functions compose
with no check of the consumer's own in between. What the second call then computes on is
`returned_values_read_back_unchanged`.

theorems.name: returned_values_read_back_unchanged
theorems.statement:
returned_values_read_back_unchanged [Discriminators] (m : Js.Module) (hm : Compile.compileProgram program = Except.ok m)
  (v : Value) (ty : Ty) (b : Nat) (d : Js.TyDesc) (hd : Compile.tyDesc program b ty = Except.ok d)
  (hv : Value.hasTy program v ty = true) : Js.normTy [] (encodeAt program ty v) d = encodeValue v
theorems.doc:
The other half of composing two calls: the second entry does not merely accept what the first handed
back, it reads it back as the value the first one returned. Together with
`returned_values_pass_the_entry_check` that is the whole of what the crossing costs — what
`decl_correct` says the first call hands back is accepted, and rebuilt as the value it encodes. A
dictionary walked out to a plain object becomes the `Map` the body works in again, and nothing else
moves.

theorems.name: steps_agree
theorems.statement:
steps_agree (fn : String) (d : Decl) (args : List Value) (hd : program.find? fn = some d)
  (hpub : d.paramsCheckable = true) :
  ∃ n, ∀ (bound : Nat), n ≤ bound → stepCall program bound fn args = evalCall program fn args
theorems.doc:
The small-step machine, given enough steps, answers exactly as `eval` does every call whose arguments
the entry check has a shape to read — which is every exported function, and every internal one that takes
no function.

theorems.name: no_rate_is_no_tax
theorems.statement: no_rate_is_no_tax (amount : Int) : taxOn amount 0 = 0
theorems.doc: Nothing is taxed at a rate of zero, whatever the amount.

theorems.name: a_refund_is_taxed_as_the_charge
theorems.statement: a_refund_is_taxed_as_the_charge (amount rate : Int) : taxOn (-amount) rate = -taxOn amount rate
theorems.doc:
A refund is taxed exactly as the charge it reverses: the tax on a negative amount is the tax on the
positive one, negated. Rounding a half away from zero is what holds this; rounding a half upwards, as
JavaScript's `Math.round` does, would not.

theorems.name: tax_of_five_at_a_tenth
theorems.statement: tax_of_five_at_a_tenth : taxOn 5 1000 = 1 ∧ taxOn (-5) 1000 = -1
theorems.doc:
Where the tax lands exactly on a half, it goes away from zero and is not dropped: a tenth of five is
one either way round, where truncating would answer zero to both. Two amounts rather than a rule — the
symmetry above holds of truncation too, so it is this that says which way a half goes.

theorems.name: the_day_holds_the_instant
theorems.statement: the_day_holds_the_instant (ms : Int) : dayOfInstant ms * 86400000 ≤ ms ∧ ms < (dayOfInstant ms + 1) * 86400000
theorems.doc:
The day an instant is filed under is the day that holds it: the instant is at or after that day's
first millisecond and before the next day's. It is what says an instant before the epoch belongs to the
day it is inside rather than to the one after — truncating division puts the last millisecond before the
epoch in day zero, where this rules it out for every instant rather than at one.

theorems.name: shares_cover_the_cost
theorems.statement: shares_cover_the_cost (cost parties : Int) : cost ≤ shareOf cost parties * max parties 1
theorems.doc:
The shares cover the cost: what each of the parties carries, multiplied back out, is never less than
the cost itself. Rounding up is what holds it, and it holds however many parties there are, a count of
zero or less being read as one.
